lines.text: Twenty-five dots. How many pairs are exactly five units apart?
lines.caption: Twenty-five dots. How many pairs are exactly five units apart?

lines.text: There are two sneaky traps hiding in this one.
lines.caption: There are two sneaky traps hiding in this one.

lines.text: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Let's hunt them down together.
lines.caption: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Let's hunt them down together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: The twenty-five dots shown are spaced one unit apart in rows and columns.
lines.caption: The twenty-five dots shown are spaced one unit apart in rows and columns.

lines.text: How many pairs of dots are exactly five units apart?
lines.caption: How many pairs of dots are exactly five units apart?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look at them.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look at them.

lines.text: So what are we counting?
lines.caption: So what are we counting?

lines.text: A pair is just two dots. We want them exactly five units apart.
lines.caption: A pair is just two dots. We want them exactly five units apart.

lines.text: Five means the straight-line distance, as if you used a ruler.
lines.caption: Five means the straight-line distance, as if you used a ruler.

lines.text: Going from one dot to the other, or back again, is still the same pair.
lines.caption: Going from one dot to the other, or back again, is still the same pair.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! First idea: go five units straight across.
lines.caption: Welcome back! First idea: go five units straight across.

lines.text: But look. A row of five dots has only four gaps. It's just four units long!
lines.caption: But look. A row of five dots has only four gaps. It's just four units long!

lines.text: So no two dots in the same row, or the same column, are five apart.
lines.caption: So no two dots in the same row, or the same column, are five apart.

lines.text: So the pair must be on a slant. That slant is the long side of a right triangle.
lines.caption: So the pair must be on a slant. That slant is the long side of a right triangle.

lines.text: Pythagoras says: across squared, plus down squared, equals five squared.
lines.caption: Pythagoras says: across squared, plus down squared, equals five squared.

lines.text: Five squared is twenty-five. Each step is at most four, since the grid is four units wide.
lines.caption: Five squared is twenty-five. Each step is at most four, since the grid is four units wide.

lines.text: Let's make a list. Across zero leaves twenty-five for down squared. Down five is too big.
lines.caption: Let's make a list. Across zero leaves twenty-five for down squared. Down five is too big.

lines.text: Across one or two leaves twenty-four or twenty-one. Neither one is a square.
lines.caption: Across one or two leaves twenty-four or twenty-one. Neither one is a square.

lines.text: Across three leaves sixteen, which is four squared! Across four leaves nine, three squared.
lines.caption: Across three leaves sixteen, which is four squared! Across four leaves nine, three squared.

lines.text: So every pair is three and four. It's the famous three, four, five triangle!
lines.caption: So every pair is three and four. It's the famous three, four, five triangle!

lines.text: Which way can the slant point? Start at the upper dot and go down.
lines.caption: Which way can the slant point? Start at the upper dot and go down.

lines.text: Three across and four down, to the right or to the left.
lines.caption: Three across and four down, to the right or to the left.

lines.text: Or four across and three down, right or left again. That's four slants.
lines.caption: Or four across and three down, right or left again. That's four slants.

lines.text: Three across and four down needs a box three wide and four tall.
lines.caption: Three across and four down needs a box three wide and four tall.

lines.text: It fits in two spots side by side, but only one top to bottom. So two places.
lines.caption: It fits in two spots side by side, but only one top to bottom. So two places.

lines.text: The other three slants fit in two places each, just the same.
lines.caption: The other three slants fit in two places each, just the same.

lines.text: Four slants, two places each. Four times two is eight! The answer is D.
lines.caption: Four slants, two places each. Four times two is eight! The answer is D.

lines.text: Here's a second way. Visit each dot, and count its partners five units away.
lines.caption: Here's a second way. Visit each dot, and count its partners five units away.

lines.text: Take the top-left corner. It has two partners: three across, four down, or four across, three down.
lines.caption: Take the top-left corner. It has two partners: three across, four down, or four across, three down.

lines.text: The dot next to a corner, along the edge, has just one partner.
lines.caption: The dot next to a corner, along the edge, has just one partner.

lines.text: Every other dot has none. Even the middle dot is too close to everything!
lines.caption: Every other dot has none. Even the middle dot is too close to everything!

lines.text: Four corners with two each makes eight. Eight edge dots with one each makes eight more.
lines.caption: Four corners with two each makes eight. Eight edge dots with one each makes eight more.

lines.text: Eight plus eight is sixteen. But each pair got counted twice, once from each end.
lines.caption: Eight plus eight is sixteen. But each pair got counted twice, once from each end.

lines.text: Sixteen over two is eight. It matches!
lines.caption: Sixteen over two is eight. It matches!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? It's a great double-check, and it shows where sixteen comes from.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? It's a great double-check, and it shows where sixteen comes from.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Two is what you'd get if you found only one slant: three across and four down, to the right.
lines.caption: Two is what you'd get if you found only one slant: three across and four down, to the right.

lines.text: Four is what you'd get if you only drew slants going down to the right.
lines.caption: Four is what you'd get if you only drew slants going down to the right.

lines.text: Six is what you'd get by halving the twelve dots that have a partner. But corners have TWO.
lines.caption: Six is what you'd get by halving the twelve dots that have a partner. But corners have TWO.

lines.text: Sixteen counts every pair twice, once from each end. A pair is two dots, counted once.
lines.caption: Sixteen counts every pair twice, once from each end. A pair is two dots, counted once.

lines.text: And watch the fence posts! Five dots in a row make only four gaps.
lines.caption: And watch the fence posts! Five dots in a row make only four gaps.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Now the grid is six dots by six dots.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Now the grid is six dots by six dots.

lines.text: That's six rows of six dots, still one unit apart. How many pairs are exactly five units apart now?
lines.caption: That's six rows of six dots, still one unit apart. How many pairs are exactly five units apart now?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Now a row has six dots, so five gaps. Five units fit straight across!
lines.caption: Let's check. Now a row has six dots, so five gaps. Five units fit straight across!

lines.text: Each row has exactly one such pair: its two end dots. Six rows give six pairs.
lines.caption: Each row has exactly one such pair: its two end dots. Six rows give six pairs.

lines.text: The six columns add six more pairs. That makes twelve straight pairs.
lines.caption: The six columns add six more pairs. That makes twelve straight pairs.

lines.text: Now the slants. Three across, four down fits three ways side to side, two ways top to bottom.
lines.caption: Now the slants. Three across, four down fits three ways side to side, two ways top to bottom.

lines.text: Three times two is six places. The other three slants fit in six places each too.
lines.caption: Three times two is six places. The other three slants fit in six places each too.

lines.text: Four slants, six places each. That's twenty-four slanted pairs.
lines.caption: Four slants, six places each. That's twenty-four slanted pairs.

lines.text: Twelve plus twenty-four is thirty-six pairs!
lines.caption: Twelve plus twenty-four is thirty-six pairs!

lines.text: If you found thirty-six, amazing work! Did you remember the straight ones?
lines.caption: If you found thirty-six, amazing work! Did you remember the straight ones?

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: To find pairs a set distance apart, first list the steps across and down that make it.
lines.caption: To find pairs a set distance apart, first list the steps across and down that make it.

lines.text: Then count the places each one fits, and count each pair only once.
lines.caption: Then count the places each one fits, and count each pair only once.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
